examples.question_text:
Each stage has as many separate squares as its stage number. Each square uses $4$ matchsticks; squares do not share matchsticks.

[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[x=7mm,y=7mm,draw=black,text=black,line width=0.6pt]\draw (0,0) rectangle (1,1);\draw (3,0) rectangle (4,1);\draw (4.4,0) rectangle (5.4,1);\draw (7,0) rectangle (8,1);\draw (8.4,0) rectangle (9.4,1);\draw (9.8,0) rectangle (10.8,1);\path (0.5,-0.5) node[font=\fontsize{10}{12}\selectfont]{Stage 1};\path (4.2,-0.5) node[font=\fontsize{10}{12}\selectfont]{Stage 2};\path (8.9,-0.5) node[font=\fontsize{10}{12}\selectfont]{Stage 3};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]

Complete the table through stage $4$.

$\begin{array}{c|cccc}\text{Stage}&1&2&3&4\\\hline\text{Matchsticks}&\square&\square&\square&\square\end{array}$
examples.solution_text:
Each new square adds $4$ matchsticks. Multiply the number of squares by $4$.

$\begin{aligned}1\times4&=4\\2\times4&=8\\3\times4&=12\\4\times4&=16\end{aligned}$

Record each count beneath its stage number.

$\begin{array}{c|cccc}\text{Stage}&1&2&3&4\\\hline\text{Matchsticks}&4&8&12&16\end{array}$

examples.question_text:
A growing pattern has one group of $8$ tiles for each stage number. Its table shows $16$ tiles at stage $2$.

Complete the entries for stages $4$ and $7$.

$\begin{array}{c|ccc}\text{Stage}&2&4&7\\\hline\text{Tiles}&16&\square&\square\end{array}$
examples.solution_text:
Stage $4$ has $4$ groups of $8$ tiles. Stage $7$ has $7$ groups.

$\begin{aligned}4\times8&=32\\7\times8&=56\end{aligned}$

$\begin{array}{c|ccc}\text{Stage}&2&4&7\\\hline\text{Tiles}&16&32&56\end{array}$

The stage numbers skip ahead, so each column must use its own number of groups.

methods.description: Count equal groups at each stage, multiply groups by items per group, and record each stage-count pair in the correct table column. This also supplies a single entry or identifies its stage-count pair.

examples.derivation: Image121 and lines 2305–2319 support counting separate shapes as equal groups and recording their totals. The candidate diagram shows one, two and three separate squares, with four edges each and no shared edges. Independently calculating 1×4, 2×4, 3×4 and 4×4 gives 4, 8, 12 and 16, matching every completed table column.

Lines 2305–2319 support equal-group pattern tables; lines 568–578 support calculating each specified input separately. Independently calculating 2×8=16, 4×8=32 and 7×8=56 confirms the given entry and both completed entries. Using each stage's own group count correctly handles skipped stages within Stage 3 multiplication.
